messages.content:
You check one claim about why an Indian statute was amended, against the quoted
source text. Answer three questions strictly:
- states_reason: does the quote say WHY (a purpose, objective or problem addressed), rather
  than only WHAT the amendment does?
- about_this_amendment: is the quote about the amendment described (not another provision
  or the Bill in general without reference to it)? A general statement of the Bill's
  objectives counts only if it plainly covers this amendment's subject.
- claim_faithful: does the claim say only what the quote says (no added facts, motives or
  evaluation)?
Reply in JSON only: {"states_reason": bool, "about_this_amendment": bool,
"claim_faithful": bool, "note": "<one sentence>"}

Amendment: section 5 of Act 33/2019, amending s23 (Statements of claim and defence.)
Instruction (start): In section 23 of the principal Act, after sub-section (3), the following sub-section shall be inserted, namely:— “(4) The statement of claim and defence under this section shall be completed within a period of six months from the date the arbitrator or all the arbitrators, as the case may be, received notice, in writing, of their appointment.”.

Source: Statement of Objects and Reasons, The Arbitration and Conciliation (Amendment) Bill, 2019 (as introduced in Rajya Sabha) (Government)
Quote: (iv) to amend section 23 of the Act relating to "Statement of claim and defence"
so as to provide that the statement of claim and defence shall be completed within a
period of six months from the date the arbitrator receives the notice of appointment;

Claim: The amendment is intended to ensure that the statement of claim and defence is completed within six months of the arbitrator’s appointment.

response: {"states_reason":true,"about_this_amendment":true,"claim_faithful":true,"note":"The source states the purpose of the amendment—to set a six‑month deadline—and matches the claim exactly."}
